findings.evidence: Functoriality.lean:79-100 (new lemma, with `heq` proved inline at 83-98) versus the existing dual pairs at 69/104, 147/161, 177/208; roadmap `ReductiveGroups/README.md:179-181` states the unipotent-element definition as a Layer 5 target.
findings.fix: Extract the conjugation identity as a named lemma (e.g. `GeneralLinearGroup.conj_eq_congrLinearEquiv (g h) : h * g * h⁻¹ = LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.congrLinearEquiv h.toLinearEquiv g`), derive `isSemisimple_conj_iff` from it, and add the dual `@[simp] isUnipotent_conj_iff` from `isUnipotent_congrLinearEquiv_iff`; list both in the module docstring.
findings.issue: `isSemisimple_conj_iff` is added with no `isUnipotent_conj_iff`, in a file whose entire API is paired (`isSemisimple_congrLinearEquiv_iff`/`isUnipotent_congrLinearEquiv_iff` at 69/104, `semisimplePart_congrLinearEquiv`/`unipotentPart_congrLinearEquiv` at 147/161, `comp_semisimplePart_eq_of_comp_eq`/`comp_unipotentPart_eq_of_comp_eq` at 177/208). The only hard part — `heq : h * g * h⁻¹ = congrLinearEquiv h.toLinearEquiv g`, lines 83-98 — is a private `have` inside the proof, so a consumer needing conjugation invariance of unipotence (roadmap Layer 5, `ρ_g − id` nilpotent) must re-derive those 15 lines of coercion juggling.

summary: The new conjugation-invariance lemma breaks the semisimple/unipotent pairing this file maintains everywhere else, and the reusable part of its proof (conjugation = congrLinearEquiv) is locked inside the proof body. Everything else — hidden bodies, intro/elim across module opacity, simp set, no compatibility surface — is fine.
